threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' when you mean the 'L' train; only locals know the true grit of the rails here.
Saw a guy in a bright orange onesie serenading the bus driver on the 68. Only in Brixton at 2 AM, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One rainy afternoon, I saw an old man feeding pigeons outside the Körnerpark while a group of kids danced in the puddles—classic Neukölln moment.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a bar that serves cocktails in mason jars, while the jukebox plays vinyl records from local bands no one outside Berlin knows.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they know to avoid Civic Center station at rush hour now—it's a hot mess with train delays and smoke from that BART scare.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, watched a guy pull out a sax during a 38 Geary wait, effortlessly blending notes with the screech of the bus brakes. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the bars close early, but in Gràcia, some don’t even get going until after 1 AM. The real night just starts then.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their awkward attempts at Catalan, especially when they mix up 'bon dia' and 'bona tarda'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think £4 for a flat white is outrageous—wait 'til you discover brunch spots where it'll set you back a tenner.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and a guy was passionately explaining the history of the South Circular to a half-asleep passenger. Only in London.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the guy at the corner kiosk knew my order by heart, even offered me a free coffee on a rainy day. That's when I felt at home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a 24/7 Späti that sells fresh flowers alongside your late-night döner. Pure Berlin vibes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they instinctively know to avoid 16th and Mission during rush hour, like it’s a landmine.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a sax on the 19 bus, serenading folks as they shuffled in. One lady handed him a dollar, but everyone just stared awkwardly.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists don’t realize that the best time for a quiet stroll in Plaça del Sol is just before dawn, when the street art is still fresh and the chatter hasn’t started.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still stop to take pictures of every building, especially during the golden hour. Old-timers just keep walking.
